newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: PLO urges U.N. action over Jerusalem violence.
newsitem.headline: PLO urges U.N. action over Jerusalem violence.

text.p: The Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) told the United Nations Wednesday that Israeli troops shot a Palestinian civilian to death and wounded about 160 others during protests against the opening to a tunnel in the Old City of Jerusalem.

In almost identical letters to the president of the Security Council and Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, PLO U.N. observer Nasser al-Kidwa said he hoped the council "will take the necessary steps."
"I wish to inform you that the Israeli occupying army has today, September 25, 1996, shot dead one Palestinian civilian and wounded approximately 160 other civilians," he wrote.

"Many Palestinians throughout the occupied Palestinian territory, including Jerusalem, were taking part in demonstrations in protest of the illegal, provocative action of opening the tunnel under the Western Wall of al-Aqsa Mosque," he added.
"Moreover, several recent statements by Israeli officials have indicated an intention to continuously challenge international legitimacy and Israel's obligations as an occupying power."
Al-Kidwa said: "The events of today increase the urgency of the matter, and I trust that the Security Council will take the necessary steps in this regard."

The protests are over a 500-yard (488-metre) Israeli-dug tunnel along excavated parts of the Western Wall, or Wailing Wall, Judaism's holiest shrine, which is also a retaining wall for the mosque compound known as Haram al-Sharif on which stands the al-Aqsa mosque, Islam's third holiest shrine.

Wednesday's letters followed notes from al-Kidwa to the council president and the secretary-general on Tuesday concerning the opening of the tunnel entrance, and on Monday about Israel's settlement policy.
